chapter: Coleman Hawkins, Bernie Young and doubling on tenor
title: Meeting Coleman Hawkins and Hawk's cello and clarinet
summary: Hawkins heard Caldwell's clarinet style in Chicago and invited him to join; they discuss Hawkins's cello training and why Caldwell settled on tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Then Hawk came through before I left with Mamie, slap tonguing and I got stuck playing with the tenor. Hawk was (unin- telligible). He was crazy about my clarinet style. I said-- he said to me, said, hey, say, why don't you come on and join us? I said, well, Hawk --
Is this when you first met him?
First met him, yeah, when I first
met Hawk.
Was he -- I mean when you first heard him, was he still playing the 'cello?
You know, he learned 'cello there in Chicago University in music. He studied there in Chicago for a while.
He did?
Yes, he did.

Well, you know that a funny thing -- I think it was when Harry Carney died. I was at that funeral home when the first person (unintelligible) -- well, he's a sax -- an old saxophone player. Lives We used to go out in Long Island. And I was talking to him, and he said, I remember Hawk playing 'cello with Raymond Smith.
He could play cello. He used to double on cello.
Did you ever see him play it?
Sure.
You did?
Yeah. And we --
(Simultaneous remarks)
Did he just play sort of straight? I mean --
Boy, he went to school on it, and he played it first after he studied at the University of --

Chicago University of Music, and he learned -- his instrument was cello, piano and cello. No, he could arrange them when But Hawk sometimes was a little lazy he wanted to. (Unintelligible), you know, and he could play a good clarinet. Lot of people didn't know that, but he could.
But he just laid it down.
He just didn't want to bother with it.
Yeah.

I said, Bean -- we used to call him Bean for short -- if we could call him -- well, I always called him Hawk. I said, "hey Bean" (unintelligible), why don't you play the clarinet?" He said, "that's why I asked you to join us when I met you in Chicago. He said, we liked your style because you was swinging with the clarinet." So I was doubling on — . Mainly I was doubling from the alto to the tenor and -- but we got in New York, and I sort of worked with from alto Benny. And I stayed on alto and then switched to baritone and tenor. So I got tired of switching from one instrument to the other, so I said, well, I'm not going to switch back, alto because Cab wanted me on also. I said, no, I'm not (unintelligible) down at the Nest Club working with fellows, you know, names that you all know, said, I'm going to stay on tenor.
